f.title: Provide Medication Guides for both new and refill prescriptions
f.statement: Part 208 sets requirements for patient labeling (Medication Guides) for human prescription drug and biological products that FDA determines pose a serious and significant public health concern requiring distribution of FDA-approved patient information; it applies primarily to outpatient products and applies to new prescriptions and refill prescriptions.
f.clause: § 208.1(a) Scope and purpose.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

rows.actor: Manufacturer (applicant) of a drug product requiring a Medication Guide; distributors, packers and authorized dispensers
rows.quote:
(a) This part sets forth requirements
for patient labeling for human prescription drug products, including biological products, that the Food and
Drug Administration (FDA) determines
pose a serious and significant public
health concern requiring distribution
of FDA-approved patient information.
It applies primarily to human prescription drug products used on an outpatient basis without direct supervision by a health professional. This
part shall apply to new prescriptions
and refill prescriptions.
rows.location: § 208.1(a) Scope and purpose.

f.title: Expect a Medication Guide requirement when FDA finds one of the 208.1(c) circumstances
f.statement: Patient labeling will be required if FDA determines that patient labeling could help prevent serious adverse effects; that the product has serious risks (relative to benefits) of which patients should be aware because the information could affect their decision to use or continue the product; or that the product is important to health and patient adherence to directions is crucial to its effectiveness.
f.clause: § 208.1(c) Scope and purpose.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

rows.actor: Manufacturer (applicant) of a drug product requiring a Medication Guide
rows.quote:
(c) Patient labeling will be required
if the FDA determines that one or
more of the following circumstances
exists:
(1) The drug product is one for which
patient labeling could help prevent serious adverse effects.

(2) The drug product is one that has
serious risk(s) (relative to benefits) of
which patients should be made aware
because information concerning the
risk(s) could affect patients’ decision
to use, or to continue to use, the product.
(3) The drug product is important to
health and patient adherence to directions for use is crucial to the drug’s effectiveness.
rows.location: § 208.1(c) Scope and purpose.
rows.review_note: Template gaps 2026-11-23, extractor. FDA determination criteria; recorded as a scope row.

f.title: Treat the applicant (or biologics manufacturer) as the manufacturer responsible for the Medication Guide
f.statement: For a drug product that is not a biological product, manufacturer means both the manufacturer described in 201.1 and the applicant described in 314.3(b); for a biological product, the manufacturer described in 600.3(t).
f.clause: § 208.3(g) Definitions.

f.title: Apply the definition of "serious risk or serious adverse effect"
f.statement: Serious risk or serious adverse effect means an adverse drug experience, or the risk of such an experience, as defined in 310.305, 312.32, 314.80 and 600.80.
f.clause: § 208.3(k) Definitions.

rows.location: § 208.3(k) Definitions.

f.title: Write the Medication Guide in English, in nontechnical language, without promotional tone
f.statement: The Medication Guide shall be written in English, in nontechnical, understandable language, and shall not be promotional in tone or content.
f.clause: § 208.20(a)(1) Content and format of a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

f.title: Keep the Medication Guide scientifically accurate and consistent with the approved professional labeling
f.statement: The Medication Guide shall be scientifically accurate and shall be based on, and shall not conflict with, the approved professional labeling under 201.57, although its language need not be identical to the corresponding sections.
f.clause: § 208.20(a)(2) Content and format of a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

corresponds.
rows.location: § 208.20(a)(2) Content and format of a Medication Guide.

f.title: Make the Medication Guide specific and comprehensive
f.statement: The Medication Guide shall be specific and comprehensive.
f.clause: § 208.20(a)(3) Content and format of a Medication Guide.

f.title: Use at least 10-point type in the Medication Guide
f.statement: The letter height or type size shall be no smaller than 10 points for all sections of the Medication Guide, except the manufacturer's name and address and the revision date.
f.clause: § 208.20(a)(4) Content and format of a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

f.title: Make the Medication Guide legible and use highlighting to emphasise key text
f.statement: The Medication Guide shall be legible and clearly presented and, where appropriate, shall use boxes, bold or underlined print or other highlighting techniques to emphasize specific portions of the text.
f.clause: § 208.20(a)(5) Content and format of a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

f.title: Show "Medication Guide" at the top and the FDA approval statement at the bottom
f.statement: The words "Medication Guide" shall appear prominently at the top of the first page, and the verbatim statement "This Medication Guide has been approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration" shall appear at the bottom.
f.clause: § 208.20(a)(6) Content and format of a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

f.title: Place the brand and established name below the title, the established name at least half the brand name height
f.statement: The brand and established or proper name shall appear immediately below the words "Medication Guide", with the established or proper name no less than one-half the height of the brand name.
f.clause: § 208.20(a)(7) Content and format of a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

f.title: Use the relevant Medication Guide headings in the specified order with the specified content
f.statement: A Medication Guide shall contain those headings listed in 208.20(b) that are relevant to the drug product and to the need for the Medication Guide, in the specified order, and each heading shall contain the specified information.
f.clause: § 208.20(b) Content and format of a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

rows.actor: Manufacturer (applicant) of a drug product requiring a Medication Guide

rows.location: § 208.20(b) Content and format of a Medication Guide.

f.title: Give brand and established names and the phonetic spelling
f.statement: The Medication Guide shall give the brand name (if any) and established or proper name (products without an established name designated by their active ingredients) and include the phonetic spelling of the brand or established name, whichever is used throughout.
f.clause: § 208.20(b)(1) Content and format of a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

rows.actor: Manufacturer (applicant) of a drug product requiring a Medication Guide
rows.quote:

established or proper name. Those
products not having an established or
proper name shall be designated by
their active ingredients. The Medication Guide shall include the phonetic
spelling of either the brand name or
the established name, whichever is
used throughout the Medication Guide.
rows.location: § 208.20(b)(1) Content and format of a Medication Guide.

f.title: Start with "What is the most important information I should know about (name of drug)?" and the specific concern
f.statement: The heading "What is the most important information I should know about (name of drug)?" shall be followed by a statement describing the particular serious and significant public health concern that created the need for the Medication Guide.
f.clause: § 208.20(b)(2) Content and format of a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

rows.actor: Manufacturer (applicant) of a drug product requiring a Medication Guide
rows.quote:
(2) The heading, ‘‘What is the most
important information I should know
about (name of drug)?’’ followed by a
statement describing the particular serious and significant public health concern that has created the need for the
Medication Guide.
rows.location: § 208.20(b)(2) Content and format of a Medication Guide.

f.title: Describe what the patient should do or consider because of the concern
f.statement: The statement should describe specifically what the patient should do or consider because of that concern, such as weighing particular risks against benefits, avoiding particular behaviors, observing certain events (symptoms, signs) that could prevent or mitigate a serious adverse effect, or engaging in particular behaviors such as adhering to the dosing regimen.
f.clause: § 208.20(b)(2) Content and format of a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

rows.actor: Manufacturer (applicant) of a drug product requiring a Medication Guide

rows.location: § 208.20(b)(2) Content and format of a Medication Guide.

f.title: Include "What is (name of drug)?" with indications from the professional labeling only
f.statement: The heading "What is (name of drug)?" shall be followed by a section identifying the product's indications for use; the Medication Guide may not identify an indication unless it is in the indications and usage section of the professional labeling under 201.57.
f.clause: § 208.20(b)(3) Content and format of a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

rows.actor: Manufacturer (applicant) of a drug product requiring a Medication Guide

rows.location: § 208.20(b)(3) Content and format of a Medication Guide.

f.title: Optionally explain the disease and the benefit of treating it
f.statement: In appropriate circumstances, the "What is (name of drug)?" section may also explain the nature of the disease or condition the product treats and the benefit(s) of treating it.
f.clause: § 208.20(b)(3) Content and format of a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

rows.location: § 208.20(b)(3) Content and format of a Medication Guide.

f.title: Include "Who should not take (name of drug)?" with contraindications and what to do
f.statement: The heading "Who should not take (name of drug)?" shall be followed by information on the contraindications, and the Medication Guide shall contain directions on what to do if any contraindication applies, such as contacting the licensed practitioner or discontinuing use.
f.clause: § 208.20(b)(4) Content and format of a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

the licensed practitioner or discontinuing use of the drug product.
rows.location: § 208.20(b)(4) Content and format of a Medication Guide.

f.title: Include "How should I take (name of drug)?" with dosing, administration, overdose and missed-dose information
f.statement: The heading "How should I take (name of drug)?" shall be followed by information on proper use, such as the importance of adhering to dosing instructions, special administration instructions important to safety or effectiveness, what to do in case of overdose, and what to do if a dose is missed (where data support the advice and wrong behavior could cause harm or lack of effect).
f.clause: § 208.20(b)(5) Content and format of a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

rows.actor: Manufacturer (applicant) of a drug product requiring a Medication Guide
rows.quote:

f.title: Include "What should I avoid while taking (name of drug)?" with activities, substances and pregnancy and nursing risks
f.statement: The heading "What should I avoid while taking (name of drug)?" shall be followed by specific, important precautions patients should take, including a statement of activities, drugs, foods or other substances to avoid, and statements of the known specific, important risks to mothers and fetuses in pregnancy and to nursing infants.
f.clause: § 208.20(b)(6)(i)-(iii) Content and format of a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

(such as tobacco or alcohol) that patients should avoid when using the
medication;
(ii) A statement of the risks to mothers and fetuses from the use of the drug
during pregnancy, if specific, important risks are known;
rows.location: § 208.20(b)(6)(i)-(iii) Content and format of a Medication Guide.

f.title: State pediatric, geriatric and other special-population precautions under "What should I avoid"
f.statement: The precautions section shall also include a statement about pediatric risks and about geriatric risks where the product has specific hazards in those patients, and a statement of any special precautions for safe and effective use in other identifiable patient populations.
f.clause: § 208.20(b)(6)(iv)-(vi) Content and format of a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

(v) A statement about geriatric risks,

(vi) A statement of special precautions, if any, that apply to the safe
and effective use of the drug product in
other identifiable patient populations.
rows.location: § 208.20(b)(6)(iv)-(vi) Content and format of a Medication Guide.

f.title: Include "What are the possible or reasonably likely side effects?" with serious or frequent reactions and dependence risk
f.statement: The heading "What are the possible or reasonably likely side effects of (name of drug)?" shall be followed by a statement of the adverse reactions reasonably likely to be caused by the product that are serious or occur frequently, and a statement of the risk, if any, of patients developing dependence.
f.clause: § 208.20(b)(7)(i)-(ii) Content and format of a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

rows.location: § 208.20(b)(7)(i)-(ii) Content and format of a Medication Guide.

f.title: Include the verbatim statement inviting patients to report side effects to FDA
f.statement: For drug products approved under section 505 of the act, the side effects section shall include the verbatim statement: "Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088."
f.clause: § 208.20(b)(7)(iii) Content and format of a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

f.title: Include the general statements on off-label prescribing and not sharing the medicine
f.statement: The general information section shall include the verbatim statement "Medicines are sometimes prescribed for purposes other than those listed in a Medication Guide", followed by a statement that patients should ask health professionals about concerns and a reference to the availability of professional labeling, and a statement that the product should not be used for another condition or given to other persons.

f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

f.title: Give the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer or distributor
f.statement: The Medication Guide shall give the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer or distributor (for a non-biological product) or of the manufacturer or distributor (for a biological product); the dispenser's name and place of business may also be included.
f.clause: § 208.20(b)(8)(iii) Content and format of a Medication Guide.

f.title: Show the most recent revision date after the last section
f.statement: The date, identified as such, of the most recent revision of the Medication Guide shall be placed immediately after the last section.

f.title: Additional headings and subheadings may be added where appropriate
f.statement: Additional headings and subheadings may be interspersed throughout the Medication Guide, if appropriate.
f.clause: § 208.20(b)(9) Content and format of a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

rows.quote: (9) Additional headings and subheadings may be interspersed throughout the Medication Guide, if appropriate.

f.title: Obtain FDA approval of the Medication Guide before distributing it
f.statement: The manufacturer of a drug product for which a Medication Guide is required shall obtain FDA approval of the Medication Guide before it may be distributed.
f.clause: § 208.24(a) Distributing and dispensing a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

rows.location: § 208.24(a) Distributing and dispensing a Medication Guide.

f.title: Make Medication Guides available in sufficient numbers, or the means to produce them, for every patient
f.statement: Each manufacturer who ships a container of a drug product requiring a Medication Guide is responsible for ensuring Medication Guides are available for distribution to patients, either by providing Medication Guides, or the means to produce them, in sufficient numbers to distributors, packers or authorized dispensers so the dispenser can provide one to each patient receiving a prescription.
f.clause: § 208.24(b) Distributing and dispensing a Medication Guide.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

f.title: Distributor or packer: pass Medication Guides (or the means to produce them) to each dispenser it ships to
f.statement: Each distributor or packer that receives Medication Guides, or the means to produce them, from a manufacturer shall provide them to each authorized dispenser to whom it ships a container of the drug product.

f.title: Label containers to instruct dispensers to provide the Medication Guide and say how it is provided
f.statement: The label of each container or package (where the container label is too small) of a drug product requiring a Medication Guide shall instruct the authorized dispenser to provide a Medication Guide to each patient to whom the product is dispensed and state how it is provided, prominently and conspicuously.
f.clause: § 208.24(d) Distributing and dispensing a Medication Guide.

f.title: Authorized dispenser: give the Medication Guide directly to each patient at dispensing
f.statement: Each authorized dispenser of a prescription drug product requiring a Medication Guide shall, when the product is dispensed to a patient (or the patient's agent), provide a Medication Guide directly to each patient (or agent) unless an exemption applies under 208.26.

f.title: Applicant may request exemption or deferral of Medication Guide content or format requirements
f.statement: An applicant may submit a written request that FDA exempt or defer any Medication Guide content or format requirement, except those in 208.20(a)(2) and (a)(6), on the basis that it is inapplicable, unnecessary or contrary to patients' best interests.
f.clause: § 208.26(a) Exemptions and deferrals.
f.exceptions: Requirements in 208.20(a)(2) and (a)(6) cannot be exempted or deferred

f.title: Send exemption or deferral requests to the reviewing FDA division
f.statement: Requests from applicants should be submitted to the director of the FDA division responsible for reviewing the marketing application, or for a biological product to the application division in the office with product responsibility.
f.clause: § 208.26(a) Exemptions and deferrals.

f.title: Authorized dispenser: provide the Medication Guide to any patient who asks, even if the prescriber directed otherwise
f.statement: The authorized dispenser of a prescription drug product subject to part 208 shall provide a Medication Guide to any patient who requests information when the drug product is dispensed, regardless of any direction by the licensed practitioner that the Medication Guide not be provided.
f.clause: § 208.26(b) Exemptions and deferrals.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

f.title: Prescriber may direct that a Medication Guide not be given to a particular patient
f.statement: If the prescribing licensed practitioner determines that it is not in a particular patient's best interest to receive a Medication Guide because of significant concerns about its effect, the practitioner may direct that the Medication Guide not be provided to that patient.
f.clause: § 208.26(b) Exemptions and deferrals.
f.applicability: Human prescription drug and biological products for which FDA requires a Medication Guide

rows.location: § 208.26(b) Exemptions and deferrals.
